correctness.rationale: For every nonzero dual support functional, optimizing each leaf interval reduces the support to two affine functions of the hub value. Their slopes give five disjoint support types for nonzero leaf coefficients, and three zero-leaf-coefficient outcomes. Each proper face is a cube; unique sign/zero patterns count all proper faces. The formula and norming-set polarity follow exactly. Standard-library exhaustive facet-intersection and connected-tight-edge potential checks corroborate all face dimensions for \(2\le m\le6\); finite testing is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: In Banach geometry, the exposed dual face of an arbitrary nonzero vector is its complete set of norming functionals, so determining its combinatorial type measures intrinsic nonsmoothness. The entire natural book-graph family has cubical norming sets in every possible dimension, a closed all-dimensional stratification and cross-polytope vertex figures. These are structural global invariants, not an arbitrary small numerical count or mere recomputation of known facet totals.
